title: Arcane (Background)
summary: An optional Background that makes a vampire hard to find.

claims.text: People who try to recall an Arcane Kindred feel a vague nostalgia without detail; it is not invisibility and gives no help in a fight.
Each dot takes one die from pools used to search for the vampire, usually Perception or Investigation; it is passive, can be switched off, and does not aid Stealth.
It cannot be held alongside Status, Clan Prestige or Fame, and has no effect for vampires of Eighth Generation or stronger blood.

title: Age (Background)
summary: An optional Background for elder chronicles.

claims.text: Age measures years spent active outside torpor, so a vampire who slept may be older than the rating shows.
Each dot grants extra freebie points but costs Humanity, and the gain slows at higher ratings because the ancient learn poorly.
Age and Military Force suit elder chronicles, and Storytellers are urged to bar them where players run neonates or ancillae.

title: Military Force (Background)
summary: An optional Background for commanding troops.

claims.text: Military Force lets a character call on armed soldiers; at the upper ratings that means an elite company of about a hundred hardened troops, and beyond it special weapons or national forces.
Sense the Sin: Perception + Empathy against the target's Self-Control + 4; one success shows a weak Virtue or Willpower, more uncover secrets, and three or more a core Derangement or old trauma.

Fear of the Void Below: after Sense the Sin, Wits + Intimidation against Courage + 4 brings trembling, then flight like Rötschreck, then fainting for the scene; Kindred resist with Courage against the Baali's Willpower.

Conflagration: each blood point spent makes black fire worth one die of aggravated damage, aimed with Dexterity + Occult at difficulty 6; it fades at the end of the turn and provokes Rötschreck like ordinary flame.
Psychomachia: after Sense the Sin, the target rolls the lowest Virtue at difficulty 6 or faces a phantom from their own darkness; a botch means frenzy or possession, and all harm from it is illusory.
The Embrace cuts a werewolf off from the soul of the world; about a dozen such beings exist at once, and most end by suicide.
An Abomination keeps old Gifts and rites, but only Wyrm-rites work and only Banes will teach new Gifts.
It cannot spend blood in the same turn it spends or rolls Gnosis or Rage, and it lives in a lasting, crippling despair.

title: Vampires and Wraiths
summary: How the undead notice the Restless.

claims.text: Few Kindred go a century without drawing a wraith's notice, usually by making one; necromancers meet them more often.
Seeing past the Shroud needs the first level of the Ash Path; Auspex 3 or more may allow a fleeting glimpse at the Storyteller's call.

title: Changelings and Kindred Blood
summary: What the Embrace and vitae do to the fae.

claims.text: An Embraced changeling loses the fae nature and becomes an ordinary vampire, though often an odd one.
Changelings can be made ghouls and blood bound; a changeling ghoul carries two permanent points of Banality while Kindred blood remains.

title: The Manus Nigrum (Revised account)
summary: The Black Hand as an older Revised source tells it.

claims.text: In this account the group grew into a Gehenna cult of mortals and vampires that wished to speed the Antediluvians' return and a new age of magic under their rule.
Over time the vampires came to control the human magicians, and according to survivors most magicians left around 500 BC.

title: Enoch and the Aralu
summary: The cult's city and the tombs beneath it.

claims.text: Many of the cult's eldest Eastern members and its mystics settled in Enoch, far from most wraiths, studying its art for clues to the Antediluvians.
Deep in Enoch's foundations lay four tombs marked Aralu, which inscriptions and sent dreams suggested might hold Antediluvians.

title: Lineages of the Manus Nigrum
summary: Assamite antitribu and True Brujah in the cult.

claims.text: A few Assamites helped found the cult and drew recruits after the Tremere curse, casting themselves as guardians of kin who fled to the Sabbat.
The True Brujah claim descent from Brujah untouched by Troile, who slew the founder; they differ from the clan in Disciplines and outlook, and some in the cult think they rose later by diablerie.
